itinerary.title: Luang Prabang: Temples, Waterfalls & Slow Riverside Days (Solo, Vegetarian)
itinerary.summary: A 4-day solo culture-and-nature loop through the UNESCO-listed old town of Luang Prabang — golden-roofed wats, teak shophouses and French-Indochine shutters under a backdrop of green mountains, exactly as the old capital is described. Mornings are for temples and markets, afternoons for waterfalls, craft villages and the Mekong, evenings for the night market and vegetarian buffets. Everything is walkable or a short tuk-tuk ride, and the plan leans on cheap local food (Luang Prabang is very veg-friendly: bamboo-soup stalls, the night-market vegetarian buffet, and Lao coffee) to stay inside ¥100–250/day. Budget notes: guesthouse dorm/private room ~¥60–110/night, meals ¥15–40, temple tickets ¥8–20, shared tuk-tuk to waterfalls ¥30–60. Bring a sarong for temple visits and cash (kip) for markets.

itinerary.title: Luang Prabang: Temples, Waterfalls & Mekong Calm (Solo, Vegetarian)
itinerary.summary: A 4-day solo culture-and-nature loop through the UNESCO-listed old town of Luang Prabang, where golden-roofed wats sit beneath teak balconies and French-Indochine shutters, backed by green mountains and the Mekong. Mornings are for temples and markets, afternoons for waterfalls and craft villages, evenings for night markets and riverside sunsets. Every food stop is vegetarian-friendly — Lao cuisine leans heavily on herbs, sticky rice, morning glory, bamboo shoots and coconut curries, and Luang Prabang has a dedicated vegan restaurant plus a famous all-you-can-eat vegetarian night-market buffet. Budget is kept tight with guesthouse-style lodging, shared songthaews and street food, comfortably inside ¥100–250/day.

itinerary.title: Tokyo Family Food & Culture Journey (6 Days, Baby-Friendly)
itinerary.summary: A relaxed six-day Tokyo itinerary for a family of four with a baby, balancing food and culture at a gentle pace. Days are grouped by neighbourhood to minimise travel and maximise stroller-friendly stops: historic Asakusa and Ueno's museums and markets, the Imperial Palace and Nihonbashi/Ginza food halls, Meiji Shrine and Shibuya/Harajuku, Toyosu's teamLab and Odaiba's open waterfront, and finally Shinjuku's gardens and viewpoints with a food-street evening. Each day mixes temples, gardens, markets and family-friendly dining within the ¥500–1500 per person daily budget, with plenty of parks, indoor alternatives and short walking legs suited to a baby.

itinerary.title: Tokyo Family Food & Culture Journey — 6 Days with a Baby
itinerary.summary: A relaxed six-day Tokyo itinerary built for a family of four travelling with a baby, balancing food and culture at a gentle pace. Days are grouped by neighbourhood so you spend less time on trains and more time eating, wandering and letting the little one nap. Expect temple streets and market breakfasts in Asakusa and Tsukiji, museum and park mornings in Ueno, shrine-and-city-view afternoons in Shibuya and Harajuku, a modern-art and waterfront day in Toyosu and Odaiba, and a green, slow-paced finale around Shinjuku and the old Yanaka lanes. All stops are chosen to be stroller-friendly, with short walking hops, indoor backup options and plenty of casual, budget-friendly eating spots so each person stays comfortably within ¥500–1500 per day.

itinerary.title: Faroe Islands Family Adventure: 5 Days of Waterfalls, Sea Cliffs & Sheep-Country Villages
itinerary.summary: A gentle-paced 5-day loop for a family of four with a baby, built around short drives, stroller-friendly viewpoints and boat trips rather than long mountain hikes. Base yourself in Tórshavn (Hotel Tórshavn, central and lift-equipped) and day-trip out to Vágar's Múlafossur waterfall, the bird cliffs of Vestmanna, and the storybook villages of Saksun and Gjógv. The Faroes are never more than 5 km from the ocean, and the countryside is steep, green and wind-swept — so this plan swaps summit hikes for coastal lookouts, paved paths and indoor warm-up stops. Budget ¥400–900 per person per day covers a shared rental car, guesthouse/hotel rooms, self-catered breakfasts and one restaurant meal a day. Accessibility notes: Faroese turf-roof villages have gravel lanes and uneven grass, so bring a carrier as backup to the stroller; the Vestmanna boat and the Vágar tunnels are fully step-free. Weather changes hourly — keep one flexible day for a rain-plan swap.

itinerary.title: Faroe Islands Family Adventure — 5 Days of Waterfalls, Cliffs & Sea Air
itinerary.summary: A slow-paced, stroller-friendly loop around the Faroe Islands for a family of four with a baby. The plan keeps driving legs short (the whole archipelago is only ~5 km from the ocean at any point), favours paved or boardwalk viewpoints over steep scrambles, and mixes big-nature highlights — the Fossá waterfall in Eiði, the Klaksvík fjord, the Mjóvanes lighthouse — with cosy indoor time in Tórshavn for nap schedules and rainy North Atlantic afternoons. Costs are per person per day and stay inside the ¥400–900 band by self-catering breakfasts, using the excellent local supermarkets, and picking one paid activity per day. Accessibility notes: all viewpoints listed have short, level approaches or can be viewed from the car park; the Vestmanna and Saksun boat/hillside options are flagged as optional for the adults while one parent stays with the baby. Pack layers, a rain cover and a carrier — paths are often grass or gravel, and weather turns fast.
